hook_text: A hole so big that people on the other side look like ants.
clip_script: Kimberley, the Big Hole. Dug largely by hand from 1871, looking for diamonds. Today, mining goes further. Strip mining peels off soil to reach coal near the surface. Open pits dig huge stepped holes, with trucks the size of houses on spiral roads. And shaft mining drops a steel cage into the dark, to tunnels deep underground. South Africa's deepest gold mines reach about four kilometres down. How deep is the mineral? That decides the mine.
visual_style: Whiteboard cross-section of the ground: a shallow strip mine, a stepped open pit, then a shaft going down and down to tunnels.
mood: Adventurous and awe-filled, like exploring underground.
pacing: Starts at the surface and goes deeper with each step.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a cross-section of the four types of mines.
